npcs.name: Mara Thimble
npcs.voice: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
barks: Tide's kind today. Don't waste it talking to me.
Butterperch fry up lovely. Not that I'd know. I'm far too busy.
If you see a light out past the Teeth, don't row toward it. Just… don't.
Your rod's older than you are. Treat it gently.
turned: You've the look of someone I've sold a rod to. I haven't, have I? No. Never mind me.
I wrote your name in the book this morning, before you'd said it. Odd, that.
Somebody's been at my prices in the night. Everything's back where it started.

npcs.name: Pell
npcs.voice: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
barks: High water at a quarter past never. Low water just after you've forgotten.
The lamp remembers. That's the trouble with lamps.
Mind the second moon. It minds you.
turned: Tide's turned. You'll have noticed. Nobody else will.
You again. For the first time.
The bell's quiet this morning. That's how you know it rang.

npcs.name: Wick
npcs.voice: excited young child, quick and breathless
barks: I'm drawing a fish with nine eyes. No, ten. It keeps changing.
Biscuit ate my blue crayon. Now everything's a bit green.
Did you know fish dream? I asked one. It said yes.
turned: I drew you yesterday. But I only met you today. Look, it's even got your hat.
Biscuit knows you. Biscuit doesn't know anybody.
Everything's new again. I like new. I think I've liked it lots of times.

npcs.name: Dr. Ines Calloway
npcs.voice: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
barks: Fourteen paces from the hut to the jetty. Yesterday it was twelve. I have not grown shorter.
Do not lean on the theodolite. It is pointing at something, and I should like to know what.
The frogs stop all at once, you know. Every evening. As if somebody had raised a hand.
turned: Have we met? No. And yet I have left room for you in the margin. How very like me.
My notebook has your catches in it, dated next week. I shall assume I was being optimistic.

npcs.name: Mara's packet box
barks: A stout sea crate with M.T. stencilled on the front. A note is pinned inside the lid: 'Fish in, coins out. Stall prices. Don't ask me how. M.'
